the: used before a noun to refer to a specific or already-known thing
The cat sat quietly on the windowsill all afternoon.
cost: the amount of money needed to buy, do, or produce something
The cost of the renovation was far higher than the family expected.
of: used to show belonging, origin, or a relationship between two things
The cover of the book was torn at the corner.
why: Why does the air above a city stay warm long after sunset?
deep: positioned far down from the surface
Tree roots often grow deep into the soil to find water.
work: activity involving effort, especially to earn a living or achieve something
The difference is not impatience on one side; it is what is doing the work.
is: present tense (he/she/it) of the verb be
The library is open until nine o'clock every evening.
profound: very great or intense; showing deep understanding
The loss had a profound effect on the whole community.
by: indicating the agent, method, or proximity of something
The letter was written by hand and delivered by courier.
continuous: happening without a break or interruption
The factory runs on a continuous production line around the clock.
in: expressing location inside or within something
The keys are in the top drawer of the desk.
modern: relating to the present time; new in style or method
The museum combines a historic building with a modern glass extension.
open-plan: describing a large indoor space with few or no interior walls
The startup's open-plan office encourages employees to talk freely.
office: a room or building where people do administrative work
She spends most of her day working in a small office.
or: used to link alternatives or possibilities
Would you like tea or coffee with your breakfast?
digital: using computer technology to store or process information
Most photographs today are stored in digital form rather than on film.
communication: the act of sharing or exchanging information or ideas
Good communication between teammates prevented any confusion during the match.
streams: small, narrow rivers of flowing water
Several small streams trickle down from the mountains after rain.
has: has; present tense of have, third person singular
The library has extended its opening hours during exam season.
been: past participle of be, used to show a completed state or experience
They have been friends since primary school.
as: used to compare, or to mean 'while' or 'because'
As the sun set, the temperature dropped quickly.
professional: relating to a skilled and paid occupation; showing high competence
She gave a very professional presentation despite her nerves.
instant: happening immediately, or, of food, quickly prepared
She made a cup of instant coffee before the meeting started.
notifications: messages that alert someone to new information, e.g. on a phone
He turned off notifications so he could focus on studying.
email: a message sent electronically between computers or phones
She sent an email to confirm the meeting time.
threads: thin strands of thread, or connected lines of discussion
The tailor sewed the button back on with a few careful threads.
and: used to connect words, phrases, or clauses
We packed sandwiches, fruit, and water for the long hike.
real-time: happening and shown immediately, without delay
The app shows real-time updates on flight delays and gate changes.
dashboard: a display or panel showing a set of key measurements or indicators
bảng điều khiển, bảng chỉ số
The company dashboard tracks sales, costs, and customer satisfaction in real time.
compete: try to win or gain something that others also want
Dozens of runners will compete for the top prize this weekend.
for: intended to belong to, or be given to, someone or something
She bought a small gift for her best friend.
our: Our house is the third one on the left side of the street.
yet: The sun has set, the traffic has thinned, and yet the air refuses to cool.
psychologists: people who study or treat the human mind and behaviour
Psychologists have studied how sleep affects memory for decades.
increasingly: more and more as time goes on
Remote work has become increasingly common since the pandemic.
caution: great care taken to avoid danger or mistakes
Drivers should proceed with caution on the icy road.
that: used to identify a specific thing, person, or clause already mentioned
The book that you gave me last year is still on my shelf.
what: used to ask for information about something
The reason lies in what cities are actually made of.
we: used to refer to the speaker and one or more other people
We forget most of what we just learned within a day.
productive: producing good or useful results efficiently
Employees tend to be more productive after a short break.
biological: relating to living organisms and their processes
The disease has a strong biological basis linked to certain genes.
terms: words with specific meanings, or conditions of an agreement
The contract lists the terms both parties must agree to follow.
an: used before a word starting with a vowel sound to mean 'one'
She ordered an apple juice and a sandwich for lunch.
expensive: The engine burns more fuel, and on a long voyage that becomes expensive.
illusion: a false impression or belief that something is real
The painting creates an illusion of depth on a flat surface.
human: relating to or characteristic of people
con người, thuộc về con người
The robot cannot yet match human judgment in complex situations.
structurally: in a way relating to how something is built or organised
The building is structurally sound despite its age.
incapable: The old engine is incapable of reaching high speeds anymore.
parallel: extending in the same direction, always the same distance apart
The two roads run parallel to each other for several kilometers.
processing: the act of treating or preparing something through a series of steps
Food processing can remove much of the fibre found in whole grains.
tasks: pieces of work that must be done
She listed all the tasks she needed to finish before Friday.
instead: He skipped dinner and had a light snack instead.
multiple: more than one; consisting of many parts
The technician worked on multiple aircraft during his years of service.
complex: consisting of many interconnected parts; not simple
The tax system is so complex that many people hire accountants.
thoughts: plural of thought; ideas or opinions formed in the mind
Behind all these approaches lies an old idea: writing is not merely a way of recording thoughts.
simultaneously: happening or done at the same time
The two teams launched their products simultaneously last week.
brain: the organ inside the head that controls thought and body function
Reading regularly keeps the brain active and engaged.
rapid: happening in a short time or at great speed
The city has seen rapid growth in population over the last decade.
each: every one of two or more things, considered separately
Each student received a copy of the new textbook.
invisible: Radio waves are invisible but carry signals across long distances.
tax: money that people must pay to the government
The government raised tax on imported cars last year.
known: recognised or familiar to many people
The area is known for its heavy afternoon rainfall.
attention: notice, thought or interest given to something
The teacher asked the students to pay attention to the diagram.
phenomenon: a fact or event, especially one that is unusual
Lightning is a natural phenomenon that has fascinated humans for centuries.
where: It changes where the effort goes, away from the comfortable hours of reading.
fragments: small pieces broken off from something larger
Tiny fragments of glass were scattered across the floor.
remain: to continue to exist or stay in the same state
Despite the changes, ticket prices will remain the same next year.
to: expressing direction, purpose, or a recipient
The sun has set, the traffic has thinned, and yet the air refuses to cool.
prior: existing or happening before something else; earlier
She had no prior experience working in agriculture.
activity: the state of being active, or a specific action being done
Doctors recommend moderate physical activity for at least an hour daily.
executive: a senior manager responsible for running a business or organisation
The executive director explained why the exhibits challenge visitors' imagination.
function: the purpose or role that something has, or how it works
The main function of the heart is to pump blood.
on: positioned at or touching the surface of something
She placed the keys on the table by the door.
subsequent: coming after something else in time; following
The subsequent chapters explain the experiment's results in detail.
task: a piece of work that must be done
Sorting the mail was the first task of her morning shift.
over: during the whole of a period of time; more than
Prices have risen steadily over the past five years.
extended: made longer, larger, or lasting for a longer time
Under extended producer responsibility, brands pay towards recycling costs.
fragmentation: The continuous fragmentation of the workday diminishes employee satisfaction and original output.
through: moving in one side and out the other; by means of
Brick, asphalt and concrete absorb heat all day and release it slowly through the night.
sustained: continuing steadily over a long period without stopping
The choir held a long, sustained note at the end of the hymn.
individuals: The programme offers grants to individuals starting a small business.
accustomed: used to something through regular experience
She quickly became accustomed to the noise of the busy street.
chronic: persisting for a long time; long-lasting, especially of an illness
Chronic back pain forced him to change careers.
report: to give information about something officially
Witnesses are encouraged to report any suspicious activity.
subjective: based on personal opinions or feelings rather than facts
Judging a painting's beauty is a largely subjective matter.
read: looked at and understood written words
The letter was read aloud to the entire assembled family.
academic: relating to schools, colleges, or scholarly study
She published several academic papers on climate policy last year.
with: Neighbourhoods with few trees heat up fastest, and these are often the poorest districts.
intricate: The carpet was woven with an intricate pattern of flowers and vines.
without: not having; in the absence of
This arrangement lets the wheel turn into a lean without anyone touching the handlebars.
novelty: the quality of being new, original, or unusual
The novelty of the gadget wore off after a few weeks.
tools: plural of tool; devices used to carry out tasks
It has no words for the small things like kitchen tools or playground arguments.
are: present tense form of 'to be' used with you, we, they
They are planning to visit their grandparents next weekend.
training: the process of teaching or practising a skill
Anyone who has stopped training for a year and then started again will recognise the pattern.
us: used to refer to the speaker and others, as the object
The line is drawn by biology, not by us.
attenuate: Frequent interruptions attenuate the depth of critical comprehension.
